What to compare

Is there value in knowing…..



CO2e by scope comparisons:


1 ’Supplier A has the highest CO2e value from:

• Scope 1

• Scope 2

• Scope 3

• Total allocated emissions


Questionable.

• Allocated values are not really comparable. Without understanding volume.

• Hard to derive actions from scope.



2 ’Supplier A has the highest CO2e % from:

• Scope 1

• Scope 2

• Scope 3

• Total allocated emissions


Questionable

• Interesting, but can’t really judge what is good / bad based on scope proportions, and without considering volume.

• Always most emissions are likely from scope 3.



3 ’Supplier A has the reduce most CO2e value from:

• Scope 1

• Scope 2

• Scope 3

• Total allocated emissions


Questionable

as above reasons



4 ’Supplier A has the reduce most CO2e % from:

• Scope 1

• Scope 2

• Scope 3

• Total allocated emissions


Questionable

as above reasons



————————————————————————————————


CO2e by energy category comparisons:


1 ’Supplier A has the highest CO2e value from:

• Fossil fuel

• Electricity standard

• Biogenic fuels

• other purchased energy

• Renewable electricity


Questionable

• Emission values are allocated, so ‘high’ does not necessarily mean they really are high though can be interesting starting point to start investigating suppliers.



2 ’Supplier A has the highest CO2e % from:

• Fossil fuel

• Electricity standard

• Biogenic fuels

• other purchased energy

• Renewable electricity


Questionable

Proportions highlight the underlying reliance of different type of energy. iIn theory can be used to target suppliers that are still reliant on Fossil fuels.


Although basing this on CO2e will always be skewed as renewable electricity is 0 emission. So if supplier only use Fossil fuel and renewables, it would look as if they have high fossil fuel proportions.



3 ’Supplier A has the reduce most CO2e value from:

• Fossil fuel

• Electricity standard

• Biogenic fuels

• other purchased energy

• Renewable electricity


Questionable

• Volume data not accounted. Hard to draw conclusions



3 ’Supplier A has the reduce most CO2e % from:

• Fossil fuel

• Electricity standard

• Biogenic fuels

• other purchased energy

• Renewable electricity


Questionable

As above. Data shewed by missing renewable.







What to compare

Is there value in knowing…..



Energy by scope comparisons:


1 ’Supplier A has the highest energy % from:

• Scope 1

• Scope 2


Questionable

• So general that might not really be interesting or actionable.



2 ’Supplier A has the reduce most energy % from:

• Scope 1

• Scope 2

• Scope 3

• Total allocated emissions


Questionable

as above reasons



————————————————————————————————


Energy by category comparisons:


1 ’Supplier A has the highest energy % from:

• Fossil fuel

• Electricity standard

• Biogenic fuels

• other purchased energy

• Renewable electricity


Yes useful

Proportions highlight the underlying reliance of different type of energy. In theory can be used to target suppliers that are still most reliant on Fossil fuels.




2 ’Supplier A has the reduce most energy % from:

• Fossil fuel

• Electricity standard

• Biogenic fuels

• other purchased energy

• Renewable electricity


Yes useful

As above. Data shewed by missing renewable.
